record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: Can GAN training for synthetic systems and networking data be combined with simulators that encode the physical constraints of the underlying system, so that data generation benefits both from statistical learning and from domain-knowledge constraints?

evidence.quote: Learning to train GANs with simulators that can model physical constraints of systems may be a good way to combine the statistical learning properties of GANs with systems that encode domain knowledge.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ denote the space of feasible trajectories of a networked system (for example, sequences of packet arrivals, throughput measurements, or system-resource time series). Suppose there is a deterministic or stochastic simulator $S:\mathcal{U}	o\mathcal{X}$ that, given control inputs $u\in\mathcal{U}$, produces outputs respecting hard physical or protocol-level constraints encoded by a constraint set $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{X}$ (e.g., causality, conservation of bytes, queueing dynamics, link-capacity limits), so that $S(u)\in\mathcal{C}$ for all $u$. Let $\mu^*$ be an unknown distribution over $\mathcal{C}$ from which a finite sample of real networked time series is drawn.

Design a generative-adversarial framework consisting of a generator $G_	heta$, a discriminator $D_\phi$, and a coupling with the simulator $S$, together with a training objective
$$\min_	heta \max_\phi \; \mathcal{L}(G_	heta, D_\phi, S),$$
such that the induced distribution $\mu_	heta$ of generated samples satisfies the following simultaneously:

1. (Hard-constraint satisfaction) $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_	heta)\subseteq\mathcal{C}$, i.e., every generated trajectory is physically/protocol-feasible.
2. (Statistical fidelity) $\mu_	heta$ converges, in an appropriate metric (e.g., Wasserstein distance or Jensen–Shannon divergence) restricted to $\mathcal{C}$, to $\mu^*$ as the sample size and capacity grow.
3. (Strict improvement) On at least one realistic networked time-series benchmark, the framework strictly improves over both (a) a pure GAN trained without the simulator and (b) the simulator $S$ alone, with respect to a fixed downstream utility metric.

Provide such a construction together with a proof (or principled empirical demonstration) that conditions 1–3 can be met, or show that no GAN-with-simulator coupling can simultaneously achieve all three.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a forward-looking research direction about combining GAN training with physics/protocol-aware simulators for networked time-series data generation. Subsequent work on simulator-in-the-loop and physics-informed GANs (e.g., physics-informed GANs, Sim2Real GANs, hybrid model-based generative models) has explored related ideas, but no definitive, general framework specifically resolving the combination for networked-systems data with guaranteed constraint satisfaction and statistical fidelity has been established. The problem appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data
status_evidence.snippet: Posed as an open research question for future work in the area of GAN-based synthetic networked time-series data.
status_evidence.claim: The combination of GAN training with simulators encoding physical constraints is identified as an open future-work direction.
